emotional_direction.central_tension: An intimate and seemingly free goldfinch is in fact chained to its feeder; the painterly illusion makes its captivity more unsettling.

evidence_details.observation: The goldfinch looks toward the viewer with its dark eye and red face.
evidence_details.significance: Creates intimacy before the chain is discovered.

evidence_details.location: leg, feeder and hanging line, central and left lower region
evidence_details.observation: The bird is tethered to the feeder by a thin chain.
evidence_details.significance: Makes captivity visible within an otherwise tender depiction.

evidence_details.location: bird's black and yellow wing, central right
evidence_details.observation: Two thick yellow strokes on black were scratched with the brush handle.
evidence_details.significance: Shows the painter's material economy and illusionism.

evidence_details.location: right of the bird and box on pale wall
evidence_details.observation: The painted shadow suggests a real bird and feeder hanging on a wall.
evidence_details.significance: Demonstrates trompe-l'oeil depth without any synthetic motion.

evidence_details.location: middle and lower half, curved bar and box
evidence_details.observation: A feeder and curved support form the bird's domestic apparatus.
evidence_details.significance: Connects the portrait to the trained pet's daily life.
Connects the painting to the artist's last year.

emotional_direction.opening_hook: The authentic bird's gaze invites an intimate encounter before the chain changes the meaning within seven seconds.
emotional_direction.closing_payoff: Return to the entire small panel with new awareness of the tether and painterly illusion.
emotional_direction.wow_justification: The authentic tether is the revelation: apparent tenderness turns into an ethical question without a fake animated bird.
